effect: The sea-trial report shows that H4 kept reference time on a voyage and explains how it could be compared with local noon to find longitude; it does not establish that every clock would perform as well.
reaction: The distinction between a successful trial and a general guarantee was a useful qualification.

mostWorthwhile.text: The sea-trial report was most worthwhile: it connected the clock method to voyage evidence while acknowledging the remaining dispute.

leastWorthwhile.text: The first lunar combination was less satisfying because the archive's role in producing the reference-time method was not initially clear.

surprise.text: The lunar method uses the Moon's position and prepared tables to find reference time, offering an alternative to carrying a clock.

arbitrary.text: Combining an older planetary archive with new lunar readings felt somewhat indirect; the chapter explains that the archive contributes recordkeeping practice, not the readings themselves.

continue.text: I would continue: comparing two routes to longitude and their limitations made the history of navigation engaging.
